title: C++26: Reducing undefined behaviour

content_html:
Nowadays, safety is in the focus of C++. Whether it’s at committee meetings, conference talks, or hallway discussions, the topic keeps coming up. C++26 made some big steps forward in this area, and one recurring theme is the reduction of cases leading to undefined behaviour.

With the words of one of the presented proposals, “undefined behaviour has all but unbounded potential for bad program behaviour, including security leaks, data corruption, deadlocks, and so on”. The simple act of violating a precondition can silently turn a perfectly correct-looking program into one that exhibits any of these.

In today’s article, we look at how and where C++26 addresses this. A couple of these changes we have already covered on this blog, but they are worth reiterating in this context. And there is one important change we haven’t talked about yet. Let’s start with that.

P3144R2: Deleting a Pointer to an Incomplete Type Should be Ill-formed

Before C++26, deleting a pointer to an incomplete type was undefined behaviour. The only exception was when the complete class type happened to have a trivial destructor and no class-specific deallocation function. In all other cases, the compiler simply could not know what to do.

Consider this example:

1
2
3
4
5
6
7

// widget.h
struct Widget;  // forward declaration only

void deleteWidget(Widget* p) {
    delete p;  // What destructor should be called?
               // Is there a custom operator delete?
}


1
2
3
4
5

// widget.cpp
struct Widget {
    ~Widget() { /* non-trivial cleanup */ }
    static void operator delete(void* p) { /* custom deallocation */ }
};

At the point of the delete expression, the compiler doesn’t know whether Widget has a non-trivial destructor or a custom operator delete - the former is quite often the case, while the latter is relatively rare. It cannot determine at translation time whether the program has well-defined behaviour or undefined behaviour - that determination depends upon information typically available only to the linker.

P3144R2 makes deleting a pointer to an incomplete class type ill-formed. Full stop. It’s now a compilation error.

The road to ill-formed

Interestingly, this wasn’t the initial direction. Several alternatives were considered which are presented in the proposal. Let’s enumerate a few of them:

  • Deprecation first: The original plan was to deprecate such deletes and only make them ill-formed in a later standard. The fear was that going straight to ill-formed would face adoption resistance.
  • Require the compiler to do the right thing: Force the implementation to generate correct destructor calls and deallocation even for incomplete types. A nice idea, but nobody knew how to implement it efficiently.
  • Don’t call the destructor: Define the behaviour as ending the object’s lifetime without running its destructor. This was combined with the concept of erroneous behaviour (borrowed from P2795R5) and deprecation.
  • Ill-formed unconditionally: Including for types with trivial destructors. This would break some existing code that currently works fine, thanks to Hyrum’s Law.

After thorough analysis, the originally preferred solution was the deprecation path combined with erroneous behaviour. The idea was to preserve well-defined behaviour in all cases but mark the pattern as deprecated. The erroneous behaviour classification would give compilers better diagnostics, both at compile time and at runtime.

But it turned out that the committee was more courageous. The courage is based on the fact that all major compilers already warn on such deletes without even trying to determine whether the complete type would have a trivial destructor. In other words, in practice, developers were already being told not to do this. So the committee went for the simplest and most impactful choice: make it ill-formed.

If you have existing code that deletes through an incomplete type, you’ll need to make the type complete at the point of deletion. This is the right thing to do anyway - it ensures the destructor actually runs.

P2795R5: Erroneous Behaviour for Uninitialized Reads

We covered this one in detail previously, but it fits perfectly into the theme of reducing undefined behaviour, so let’s recap.

Reading an uninitialized local variable used to be undefined behaviour. Starting from C++26, it becomes erroneous behaviour - a new category that means the behaviour is well-defined but incorrect. The compiler is recommended to diagnose it.

1
2
3
4

void foo() {
    int d;  // d has an erroneous value
    bar(d); // erroneous behaviour, not UB anymore
}

Instead of the program silently doing anything (as UB permits), an uninitialized object is now initialized to an implementation-specific value. Reading it is a conceptual error that compilers are encouraged to diagnose through warnings or runtime errors.

If you intentionally want to leave a variable uninitialized for performance reasons, C++26 gives you the [[indeterminate]] attribute. But in that case, reading the variable before initialization is still undefined behaviour - you’re explicitly opting into it.

The beauty of this change is that it works just by recompiling existing code. No manual code changes needed - the compiler will tell you where you forgot to initialize variables.

P2748R5: Disallow Binding a Returned Reference to a Temporary

This one we also discussed in a dedicated article. It turns a common dangling-reference pattern from undefined behaviour into a compilation error.

Before C++26, the standard said that the lifetime of a temporary bound to the returned value in a function return statement is not extended. The temporary is simply destroyed at the end of the full-expression in the return statement. This was a recipe for dangling references.

1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8
9

auto&& f1() {
    return 42;  // was UB, now ill-formed
}

const double& f2() {
    static int x = 42;
    return x;   // implicit conversion to double creates a temporary
                // was UB, now ill-formed
}

C++26 replaces the vague “lifetime is not extended” wording with a clear rule: a return statement that binds the returned reference to a temporary expression is ill-formed. The code won’t compile. This eliminates a whole class of subtle lifetime bugs at compile time rather than letting them manifest as mysterious crashes at runtime.

P3471R4: Standard Library Hardening

The changes above are all on the language side. But C++26 also addresses safety on the library side through standard library hardening, which we covered in a dedicated article.

The idea behind hardening is simple: many standard library operations have preconditions that, when violated, lead to undefined behaviour. Accessing vector[10] when the vector has only 5 elements is undefined behaviour. So is calling front() on an empty optional, or dereferencing an invalid span index.

P3471R4 standardizes a mechanism for implementations to check these preconditions at runtime. When a check fails, the program can trap or abort instead of silently corrupting memory. It covers containers like std::vector, std::array and std::deque, views like std::span and std::string_view, and wrappers like std::optional and std::expected.

What makes this approach practical is that it’s opt-in and requires no code changes - you just recompile with hardening enabled (e.g. -fhardened in Clang and GCC). Real-world deployments report roughly 0.3% performance overhead while catching thousands of bugs. That’s a remarkable trade-off.

Conclusion

C++26 tackles undefined behaviour from multiple angles. On the language side, deleting a pointer to an incomplete type is now ill-formed, reading uninitialized variables becomes erroneous rather than undefined, and returning a reference to a temporary is a compilation error. On the library side, standard hardening gives implementations a standardized way to catch precondition violations at runtime with minimal overhead.

None of these changes require new programming paradigms or major rewrites. Most of them work simply by recompiling existing code with a C++26-conforming compiler. That’s the kind of progress that matters: making existing code safer without asking developers to change how they think.

sentences.zh: 我们之前详细介绍过这一点，但它完全符合减少未定义行为的主题，所以让我们回顾一下。

blocks.html_en: Reading an uninitialized local variable used to be undefined behaviour. Starting from C++26, it becomes erroneous behaviour - a new category that means the behaviour is well-defined but incorrect. The compiler is recommended to diagnose it.

sentences.en: Reading an uninitialized local variable used to be undefined behaviour.
sentences.zh: 读取未初始化的局部变量曾经是未定义的行为。

sentences.en: Starting from C++26, it becomes erroneous behaviour - a new category that means the behaviour is well-defined but incorrect.
sentences.zh: 从C++26开始，它变成了错误行为——一个新的类别，意味着行为定义良好但不正确。

sentences.en: The compiler is recommended to diagnose it.
sentences.zh: 建议编译器对其进行诊断。

    int d;  // d has an erroneous value
    bar(d); // erroneous behaviour, not UB anymore

sentences.en: 1 2 3 4 void foo() { int d; // d has an erroneous value bar(d); // erroneous behaviour, not UB anymore }
sentences.zh: 1 2 3 4 void foo() { int d; // d 有一个错误的值 bar(d); // 错误行为，不再是 UB }

blocks.html_en: Instead of the program silently doing anything (as UB permits), an uninitialized object is now initialized to an implementation-specific value. Reading it is a conceptual error that compilers are encouraged to diagnose through warnings or runtime errors.

sentences.en: Instead of the program silently doing anything (as UB permits), an uninitialized object is now initialized to an implementation-specific value.
sentences.zh: 程序不再默默地执行任何操作（如 UB 允许的那样），而是将未初始化的对象初始化为特定于实现的值。

sentences.en: Reading it is a conceptual error that compilers are encouraged to diagnose through warnings or runtime errors.
sentences.zh: 阅读它是一个概念性错误，鼓励编译器通过警告或运行时错误来诊断。

blocks.html_en: If you intentionally want to leave a variable uninitialized for performance reasons, C++26 gives you the [[indeterminate]] attribute. But in that case, reading the variable before initialization is still undefined behaviour - you’re explicitly opting into it.

sentences.en: If you intentionally want to leave a variable uninitialized for performance reasons, C++26 gives you the [[indeterminate]] attribute.
sentences.zh: 如果出于性能原因您有意保留变量未初始化，C++26 会为您提供 [[inminated]] 属性。

sentences.en: But in that case, reading the variable before initialization is still undefined behaviour - you’re explicitly opting into it.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，在初始化之前读取变量仍然是未定义的行为 - 您明确选择了它。

blocks.html_en: The beauty of this change is that it works just by recompiling existing code. No manual code changes needed - the compiler will tell you where you forgot to initialize variables.

sentences.en: The beauty of this change is that it works just by recompiling existing code.
sentences.zh: 这一变化的美妙之处在于它只需重新编译现有代码即可发挥作用。

sentences.en: No manual code changes needed - the compiler will tell you where you forgot to initialize variables.
sentences.zh: 无需手动更改代码 - 编译器会告诉您在哪里忘记初始化变量。

blocks.html_en: P2748R5: Disallow Binding a Returned Reference to a Temporary

sentences.en: P2748R5: Disallow Binding a Returned Reference to a Temporary
sentences.zh: P2748R5：禁止将返回的引用绑定到临时引用

blocks.html_en: This one we also discussed in a dedicated article. It turns a common dangling-reference pattern from undefined behaviour into a compilation error.

sentences.en: This one we also discussed in a dedicated article.
sentences.zh: 我们也在一篇专门的文章中讨论了这个问题。

sentences.en: It turns a common dangling-reference pattern from undefined behaviour into a compilation error.
sentences.zh: 它将常见的悬空引用模式从未定义的行为转变为编译错误。

blocks.html_en: Before C++26, the standard said that the lifetime of a temporary bound to the returned value in a function return statement is not extended. The temporary is simply destroyed at the end of the full-expression in the return statement. This was a recipe for dangling references.

sentences.en: Before C++26, the standard said that the lifetime of a temporary bound to the returned value in a function return statement is not extended.
sentences.zh: 在 C++26 之前，标准规定绑定到函数 return 语句中返回值的临时变量的生命周期不会延长。

sentences.en: The temporary is simply destroyed at the end of the full-expression in the return statement.
sentences.zh: 临时变量在 return 语句中的完整表达式末尾被简单地销毁。

sentences.en: This was a recipe for dangling references.
sentences.zh: 这是悬空引用的秘诀。

blocks.html_en: C++26 replaces the vague “lifetime is not extended” wording with a clear rule: a return statement that binds the returned reference to a temporary expression is ill-formed. The code won’t compile. This eliminates a whole class of subtle lifetime bugs at compile time rather than letting them manifest as mysterious crashes at runtime.

sentences.en: C++26 replaces the vague “lifetime is not extended” wording with a clear rule: a return statement that binds the returned reference to a temporary expression is ill-formed.
sentences.zh: C++26 用明确的规则替换了模糊的“生命周期不延长”措辞：将返回的引用绑定到临时表达式的 return 语句是格式错误的。

sentences.en: The code won’t compile.

sentences.en: This eliminates a whole class of subtle lifetime bugs at compile time rather than letting them manifest as mysterious crashes at runtime.
sentences.zh: 这消除了编译时一整类微妙的生命周期错误，而不是让它们在运行时表现为神秘的崩溃。

blocks.html_en: P3471R4: Standard Library Hardening

sentences.en: P3471R4: Standard Library Hardening
sentences.zh: P3471R4：标准库强化

blocks.html_en: The changes above are all on the language side. But C++26 also addresses safety on the library side through standard library hardening, which we covered in a dedicated article.

sentences.en: The changes above are all on the language side.
sentences.zh: 以上的变化都是在语言方面。

sentences.en: But C++26 also addresses safety on the library side through standard library hardening, which we covered in a dedicated article.
sentences.zh: 但 C++26 还通过标准库强化来解决库方面的安全问题，我们在专门的文章中对此进行了介绍。

blocks.html_en: The idea behind hardening is simple: many standard library operations have preconditions that, when violated, lead to undefined behaviour. Accessing vector[10] when the vector has only 5 elements is undefined behaviour. So is calling front() on an empty optional, or dereferencing an invalid span index.

sentences.en: The idea behind hardening is simple: many standard library operations have preconditions that, when violated, lead to undefined behaviour.
sentences.zh: 强化背后的想法很简单：许多标准库操作都有先决条件，如果违反这些先决条件，就会导致未定义的行为。

sentences.en: Accessing vector[10] when the vector has only 5 elements is undefined behaviour.
sentences.zh: 当向量只有 5 个元素时访问向量[10] 是未定义的行为。

sentences.en: So is calling front() on an empty optional, or dereferencing an invalid span index.
sentences.zh: 对空可选值调用 front() 或取消引用无效的跨度索引也是如此。

blocks.html_en: P3471R4 standardizes a mechanism for implementations to check these preconditions at runtime. When a check fails, the program can trap or abort instead of silently corrupting memory. It covers containers like std::vector, std::array and std::deque, views like std::span and std::string_view, and wrappers like std::optional and std::expected.

sentences.en: P3471R4 standardizes a mechanism for implementations to check these preconditions at runtime.
sentences.zh: P3471R4 标准化了一种实现机制，用于在运行时检查这些先决条件。

sentences.en: When a check fails, the program can trap or abort instead of silently corrupting memory.
sentences.zh: 当检查失败时，程序可以捕获或中止，而不是默默地破坏内存。

sentences.en: It covers containers like std::vector, std::array and std::deque, views like std::span and std::string_view, and wrappers like std::optional and std::expected.
sentences.zh: 它涵盖了像 std::vector、std::array 和 std::deque 这样的容器，像 std::span 和 std::string_view 这样的视图，以及像 std::optional 和 std::expected 这样的包装器。

blocks.html_en: What makes this approach practical is that it’s opt-in and requires no code changes - you just recompile with hardening enabled (e.g. -fhardened in Clang and GCC). Real-world deployments report roughly 0.3% performance overhead while catching thousands of bugs. That’s a remarkable trade-off.

sentences.en: What makes this approach practical is that it’s opt-in and requires no code changes - you just recompile with hardening enabled (e.g. -fhardened in Clang and GCC).
sentences.zh: 这种方法之所以实用，是因为它是选择性加入的，不需要更改代码 - 您只需在启用强化的情况下重新编译（例如 Clang 和 GCC 中的 -fhardened）。

sentences.en: Real-world deployments report roughly 0.3% performance overhead while catching thousands of bugs.
sentences.zh: 实际部署报告大约有 0.3% 的性能开销，同时发现了数千个错误。

sentences.en: That’s a remarkable trade-off.
sentences.zh: 这是一个了不起的权衡。

blocks.html_en: Conclusion

sentences.en: Conclusion
sentences.zh: 结论

blocks.html_en: C++26 tackles undefined behaviour from multiple angles. On the language side, deleting a pointer to an incomplete type is now ill-formed, reading uninitialized variables becomes erroneous rather than undefined, and returning a reference to a temporary is a compilation error. On the library side, standard hardening gives implementations a standardized way to catch precondition violations at runtime with minimal overhead.

sentences.en: C++26 tackles undefined behaviour from multiple angles.
sentences.zh: C++26 从多个角度处理未定义的行为。

sentences.en: On the language side, deleting a pointer to an incomplete type is now ill-formed, reading uninitialized variables becomes erroneous rather than undefined, and returning a reference to a temporary is a compilation error.
sentences.zh: 在语言方面，删除指向不完整类型的指针现在是格式错误的，读取未初始化的变量变得错误而不是未定义，并且返回对临时的引用是编译错误。

sentences.en: On the library side, standard hardening gives implementations a standardized way to catch precondition violations at runtime with minimal overhead.
sentences.zh: 在库方面，标准强化为实现提供了一种标准化方法，可以在运行时以最小的开销捕获前提条件违规。

blocks.html_en: None of these changes require new programming paradigms or major rewrites. Most of them work simply by recompiling existing code with a C++26-conforming compiler. That’s the kind of progress that matters: making existing code safer without asking developers to change how they think.

sentences.en: None of these changes require new programming paradigms or major rewrites.
sentences.zh: 这些变化都不需要新的编程范例或重大重写。

sentences.en: Most of them work simply by recompiling existing code with a C++26-conforming compiler.
sentences.zh: 其中大多数只需使用符合 C++26 的编译器重新编译现有代码即可工作。

sentences.en: That’s the kind of progress that matters: making existing code safer without asking developers to change how they think.
sentences.zh: 这就是重要的进步：使现有代码更安全，而不要求开发人员改变他们的想法。

content_html_zh:
如今，安全性是 C++ 的重点。 无论是在委员会会议、会议演讲还是走廊讨论中，这个话题都会不断出现。 C++26 在这一领域取得了一些重大进展，一个反复出现的主题是减少导致未定义行为的情况。

用所提出的提案之一的话来说，“未定义的行为几乎具有无限的潜在的不良程序行为，包括安全漏洞、数据损坏、死锁等等”。 违反先决条件的简单行为可以悄悄地将看起来完全正确的程序变成表现出其中任何一个的程序。

在今天的文章中，我们将了解 C++26 如何以及在何处解决这个问题。 我们已经在本博客中介绍了其中一些更改，但在本文中值得重申。 还有一项重要的变化我们还没有讨论过。 让我们从那开始吧。

P3144R2：删除指向不完整类型的指针应该是错误的

在 C++26 之前，删除指向不完整类型的指针是未定义的行为。 唯一的例外是完整的类类型碰巧有一个简单的析构函数并且没有特定于类的释放函数。 在所有其他情况下，编译器根本不知道该怎么做。

考虑这个例子：

1 2 3 4 5 6 7 // widget.h struct Widget; // 仅前向声明 void deleteWidget(Widget* p) { delete p; // 应该调用什么析构函数？ // 是否有自定义的删除运算符？ }

1 2 3 4 5 // widget.cpp struct Widget { ~Widget() { /* 重要的清理 */ } static void operator delete(void* p) { /* 自定义释放 */ } };

在删除表达式时，编译器不知道 Widget 是否具有重要的析构函数或自定义运算符删除 - 前者很常见，而后者相对较少。 它无法在翻译时确定程序是否具有明确定义的行为或未定义的行为 - 该确定取决于通常仅对链接器可用的信息。

P3144R2 导致删除指向不完整类类型的指针的格式不正确。 句号。 现在是编译错误。

通往不良之路

有趣的是，这并不是最初的方向。 考虑了提案中提出的几种替代方案。 让我们列举其中的一些：

  • 首先弃用：最初的计划是弃用此类删除，只会在以后的标准中使它们格式不正确。 人们担心直接采用不规范的方式会面临采用阻力。
  • 要求编译器做正确的事情：强制实现生成正确的析构函数调用和释放，即使对于不完整的类型也是如此。 这是一个好主意，但没有人知道如何有效地实施它。
  • 不要调用析构函数：将行为定义为结束对象的生命周期而不运行其析构函数。 这与错误行为（借自 P2795R5）和弃用的概念相结合。
  • 无条件格式错误：包括具有简单析构函数的类型。 由于海勒姆定律，这将破坏一些目前运行良好的现有代码。

经过彻底分析，最初首选的解决方案是弃用路径与错误行为相结合。 这个想法是在所有情况下保留明确定义的行为，但将模式标记为已弃用。 错误行为分类将为编译器提供更好的诊断，无论是在编译时还是在运行时。

但事实证明，委员会的胆子更大。 这种勇气是基于这样一个事实：所有主要编译器都已经对此类删除发出警告，甚至没有尝试确定完整类型是否有一个简单的析构函数。 换句话说，在实践中，开发人员已经被告知不要这样做。 因此，委员会采取了最简单、最有影响力的选择：使其格式不正确。

如果您有通过不完整类型进行删除的现有代码，则需要在删除时使类型完整。 无论如何，这是正确的做法 - 它确保析构函数实际运行。

P2795R5：未初始化读取的错误行为

我们之前详细介绍过这一点，但它完全符合减少未定义行为的主题，所以让我们回顾一下。

读取未初始化的局部变量曾经是未定义的行为。 从C++26开始，它变成了错误行为——一个新的类别，意味着行为定义良好但不正确。 建议编译器对其进行诊断。

1 2 3 4 void foo() { int d; // d 有一个错误的值 bar(d); // 错误行为，不再是 UB }

程序不再默默地执行任何操作（如 UB 允许的那样），而是将未初始化的对象初始化为特定于实现的值。 阅读它是一个概念性错误，鼓励编译器通过警告或运行时错误来诊断。

如果出于性能原因您有意保留变量未初始化，C++26 会为您提供 [[inminated]] 属性。 但在这种情况下，在初始化之前读取变量仍然是未定义的行为 - 您明确选择了它。

这一变化的美妙之处在于它只需重新编译现有代码即可发挥作用。 无需手动更改代码 - 编译器会告诉您在哪里忘记初始化变量。

P2748R5：禁止将返回的引用绑定到临时引用

我们也在一篇专门的文章中讨论了这个问题。 它将常见的悬空引用模式从未定义的行为转变为编译错误。

在 C++26 之前，标准规定绑定到函数 return 语句中返回值的临时变量的生命周期不会延长。 临时变量在 return 语句中的完整表达式末尾被简单地销毁。 这是悬空引用的秘诀。

1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 auto&& f1() { return 42; // 以前是 UB，现在格式错误 } const double& f2() { static int x = 42;返回x； // 隐式转换为 double 创建一个临时 // 是 UB，现在格式错误 }

C++26 用明确的规则替换了模糊的“生命周期不延长”措辞：将返回的引用绑定到临时表达式的 return 语句是格式错误的。 该代码无法编译。 这消除了编译时一整类微妙的生命周期错误，而不是让它们在运行时表现为神秘的崩溃。

P3471R4：标准库强化

以上的变化都是在语言方面。 但 C++26 还通过标准库强化来解决库方面的安全问题，我们在专门的文章中对此进行了介绍。

强化背后的想法很简单：许多标准库操作都有先决条件，如果违反这些先决条件，就会导致未定义的行为。 当向量只有 5 个元素时访问向量[10] 是未定义的行为。 对空可选值调用 front() 或取消引用无效的跨度索引也是如此。

P3471R4 标准化了一种实现机制，用于在运行时检查这些先决条件。 当检查失败时，程序可以捕获或中止，而不是默默地破坏内存。 它涵盖了像 std::vector、std::array 和 std::deque 这样的容器，像 std::span 和 std::string_view 这样的视图，以及像 std::optional 和 std::expected 这样的包装器。

这种方法之所以实用，是因为它是选择性加入的，不需要更改代码 - 您只需在启用强化的情况下重新编译（例如 Clang 和 GCC 中的 -fhardened）。 实际部署报告大约有 0.3% 的性能开销，同时发现了数千个错误。 这是一个了不起的权衡。

结论

C++26 从多个角度处理未定义的行为。 在语言方面，删除指向不完整类型的指针现在是格式错误的，读取未初始化的变量变得错误而不是未定义，并且返回对临时的引用是编译错误。 在库方面，标准强化为实现提供了一种标准化方法，可以在运行时以最小的开销捕获前提条件违规。

这些变化都不需要新的编程范例或重大重写。 其中大多数只需使用符合 C++26 的编译器重新编译现有代码即可工作。 这就是重要的进步：使现有代码更安全，而不要求开发人员改变他们的想法。
